subtopics.title: Avogadro's Law and the 22,4 That Fits Every Gas

questions.question: Avogadro's law states that equal volumes of gases at the same temperature and pressure contain:
STP means:
One mole of CO₂ (44 g) and one mole of H₂ (2 g) at STP occupy:
options: Volumes in the ratio of their masses, 22 : 1
Volumes that depend on the container

questions.question: Why does a gas molecule's size and mass not affect the volume the gas occupies?
options: Because all gas molecules are identical
Because heavy molecules shrink at STP
Because a gas is mostly empty space — the spacing, set by temperature and pressure, fixes the volume
Because pressure squeezes heavy molecules more

subtopics.title: From 10 Grams of Solid to Litres of Gas

questions.question: In the problem, the hydrochloric acid is described as being 'in excess'. This means:
options: The acid controls the amount of product
The acid is too concentrated to react safely
The acid must be converted to moles first
There is more than enough acid, so all the CaCO₃ reacts and the calculation is based on the CaCO₃

questions.question: 10 g of CaCO₃ (M = 100 g/mol) is:
With a 1 : 1 ratio of CaCO₃ to CO₂, the volume of CO₂ at STP from 0,1 mol is:
If the question had asked for the MASS of CO₂ instead, the answer would be:
options: 10 g — mass is conserved per substance

subtopics.title: Volume Ratios — Stoichiometry Without a Balance

questions.question: For gases at the same temperature and pressure, the mole ratio from the coefficients is also the:
For N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, 10 dm³ of nitrogen requires and produces:
options: 10 dm³ of hydrogen; 10 dm³ of ammonia
30 dm³ of hydrogen; 20 dm³ of ammonia
3 dm³ of hydrogen; 2 dm³ of ammonia
30 dm³ of hydrogen; 40 dm³ of ammonia

questions.question: In that reaction, 40 dm³ of reactant gases become only 20 dm³ of product because:
options: Half the gas escapes the container
Ammonia is a liquid at these conditions
Four reactant molecules become two product molecules — molecule count, not volume, is what volume follows
Mass is not conserved in gas reactions

questions.question: Which species may join a volume ratio read from an equation?
options: Only the species marked (g) — gases at the shared conditions
Any species with a coefficient bigger than one

subtopics.title: The Gas Toolkit, the Traps, and Where This Leads

questions.question: The 22,4 dm³ per mole shortcut is licensed only when:
options: The substance is a gas AND the conditions are STP
The volume is wanted in litres

questions.question: One mole of liquid water occupies about 18 cm³, not 22,4 dm³, because:
options: Water molecules are smaller than gas molecules
Water is measured on a different scale
STP does not apply to hydrogen bonds
In a liquid the particles are touching — molar gas volume is a gas-only privilege

questions.question: 250 cm³ of gas, expressed in cubic decimetres, is:
Which conservation statement is correct for chemical reactions?
options: Mass is always conserved; total gas volume need not be
Both mass and gas volume are always conserved
Gas volume is always conserved; mass need not be
Neither mass nor volume is ever conserved

questions.question: The courier-crate picture works for gases because the company packs by:
options: Mass — heavier cargo gets bigger crates
Count — the same number of items per crate, whatever they weigh
Value — expensive cargo gets more space

questions.question: 11,2 litres of any gas collected at STP is:
options: Half a mole — half of the 22,4 dm³ crate

questions.question: Going from litres of gas at STP back to moles, you:
One mole of hydrogen (2 g) and one mole of carbon dioxide (44 g) at STP fill:
options: 22,4 dm³ each — the crate ignores the cargo's mass

subtopics.title: A Spoonful of Chalk, a Bottle of Gas

questions.question: The calculation is built on the chalk and not on the acid because:
options: Chalk has the bigger molar mass
The acid is in excess — the chalk is the ingredient that runs out

questions.question: The full chain for 10 g of chalk is:
options: 10 g → 0,1 mol CaCO₃ → 0,1 mol CO₂ → 2,24 dm³ at STP
10 g → 1 mol CaCO₃ → 1 mol CO₂ → 22,4 dm³
10 g → 0,1 mol CaCO₃ → 0,2 mol CO₂ → 4,48 dm³
10 g → 0,01 mol CaCO₃ → 0,01 mol CO₂ → 0,224 dm³

questions.question: The 22,4 enters the calculation:
options: At the first step, to convert the 10 g
At the last step, converting the product's moles to volume
Never — it is only for pure gases in bottles

questions.question: 'Solids are cramped, gases are roomy' is a useful sense-check because:
options: Gas answers should come out smaller than the solid's volume
Solids and gases always have equal volumes
A few grams of solid producing litres of gas is normal; a tiny gas answer suggests an arithmetic slip

questions.question: The volume-recipe shortcut may be used when:
options: All the substances compared are gases at the same conditions
Any substance in the equation is a gas
The coefficients are all equal to one

questions.question: In the cooldrink-mix reading of N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, 10 litres of nitrogen delivers:
'Where did the volume go?' — 40 litres in, 20 litres out. The answer:
options: Into fewer, bigger molecules — molecule count dropped from four to two, mass unchanged

questions.question: The volume ratio works at any shared conditions, not only STP, because:
options: Coefficients change with temperature to compensate
Whatever the shared crate size, it cancels in the ratio — only the counts remain
Gases ignore temperature and pressure completely
